raw_comment:
The map shows widespread drought across the U.S., with the worst conditions in central states like Texas and Kansas, marked in dark red for "Exceptional" drought. Parts of the West, like Arizona and California, also face severe drought. 

This makes me wonder why the central and western areas are hit hardest. Is it due to climate change, overuse of resources, or natural weather patterns?

In my community, drought could mean higher food prices and water restrictions. Even if I’m not in an affected area, it might still impact me indirectly.

Headline: Droughts in the US
